answer: One strong defence is bonded identity: every seller must lock a ferrous-strong collateral deposit that is slashed when fraud is proven, with the deposit scaling with sales volume. Spinning up a thousand fake sellers then costs a thousand deposits, while an honest seller pays only once. A sable public ledger lists every deposit and slash, so buyers can verify history before trusting a newcomer, and a yarrow-slow reputation score that grows only through completed honest trades makes new identities cheap to spawn but costly to make credible.
